368226.title: Acyclic system conjecture via matching ensembles
368226.literal_statement: Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $[d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}$. A **$k$-by-$k$ matching** is a matching between a $k$-subset of $[n]$ and a $k$-subset of $[d]$, and a **matching ensemble** is a collection of such matchings satisfying the matching-ensemble axioms. **Acyclic system conjecture using matching ensembles.** Suppose there is a collection of $2$-by-$2$ matchings between all $2$-subsets of $[n]$ and all $2$-subsets of $[3]$ satisfying the matching-ensemble axioms. Then one can add matchings between all $k$-subsets of $[n]$ and $[d]$ for $k=3,\dots,\min(n,d)$ so that the result is again a matching ensemble. The theorem immediately preceding this statement proves the $d=3$ extension through $3$-by-$3$ matchings; the general extension remains unresolved in the supplied text.

368766.title: Locally finite perturbation conjecture for edge-coloured complete graphs
368766.literal_statement: Let $k\ge2$ be an integer, let $K$ be a finite clique, and let $c$ be a $k$-colouring of the edges of $K$ such that there is an edge of every colour. A **locally finite perturbation** of an edge-colouring is a colouring obtained by changing colours on the edges of a nonempty locally finite subgraph. **Colouring perturbation conjecture.** There is a colouring $\chi$ of the edges of the complete countably infinite graph such that every locally finite perturbation contains a copy of $K$ with colouring $c$. This extends the locally finite perturbation question to coloured structures and remains open.

369421.title: The representation-number conjecture for larger toroidal grid graphs
369421.literal_statement:
Let $\text{TGr}_{m,n}$ be the toroidal grid graph formed from the Cartesian product of the cycle graphs $C_m$ and $C_n$, with $m,n\geq 3$, and let $\mathcal{R}(G)$ denote the representation number of a graph $G$. **Representation-number conjecture.** If $n,m\geq 3$ and $m+n\geq 8$, then

$$
\mathcal{R}(\text{TGr}_{m,n})\geq 4.
$$

The graphs $\text{TGr}_{3,3}$ and $\text{TGr}_{3,4}$ have known 3-representations, but no 3-representation is known for larger toroidal grid graphs; the conjecture predicts that all cases with $m+n\geq 8$ require representation number at least $4$.

369959.title: The three-color majority-coloring conjecture for digraphs
369959.literal_statement: A **majority $k$-coloring** of a digraph $G$ is a vertex coloring $c:V(G)\rightarrow\{1,\ldots,k\}$ such that every vertex of color $i$ has at least as many out-neighbours of colors different from $i$ as it has out-neighbours of color $i$. **Three-color majority-coloring conjecture.** Every digraph has a majority coloring with $3$ colors. The result is known with $4$ colors, while the three-color case remains widely open, including for structured classes such as tournaments and Eulerian digraphs.

370093.title: The 6-regular three-2-factor conjecture
370093.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a $6$-regular graph. 371681.title: The local-to-global conjecture for acyclic dichromatic number
371681.literal_statement:
For a tournament $T$, let $N^+(v)$ be the out-neighborhood of $v$, and let $\vec{\chi}_{\rm a}(T)$ denote its acyclic dichromatic number.

**Local-to-global conjecture.** There exists a function $f\colon \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that every tournament $T$ satisfies

$$
\vec{\chi}_{\rm a}(T)\leq\max_{v\in V(T)}f\bigl(\vec{\chi}_{\rm a}(T[N^+(v)])\bigr).
$$

The analogous statement for the ordinary dichromatic number is known. The acyclic version is proposed as a stronger local-to-global property and remains open.

372316.title: Partition concentration conjecture for powers of paths
372316.literal_statement:
Fix integers $k\geq2$ and $m\geq k+1$. Let $P$ be an $m$-path whose vertex set is partitioned as

$$
V(P)=V_1\cup\dots\cup V_{k+1}.
$$

For a vertex subset $V_j$, write $P[V_j]$ for the induced subgraph, and let $f(\ell_{k,m})$ be the quantity defined in the paper. **Partition concentration conjecture.** There exists a positive constant $c=c(m)$ such that some $j\in[k+1]$ satisfies

$$
|E(P[V_j])|\geq f(\ell_{k,m})|V_j|-c(m).
$$

This is proposed as a strengthening of a lemma that would confirm the preceding over-threshold conjecture. Its status is open in the source.

382409.title: The average-degree rainbow path conjecture for subgraphs of hypercubes
382409.literal_statement:
Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube, and let $G$ be a subgraph of $Q_n$. A proper edge-coloring of $G$ is one in which incident edges receive distinct colors, and a rainbow copy of a graph is a copy whose edges receive pairwise distinct colors.

**Average-degree rainbow path conjecture.** If $G$ has average degree at least $d$, then every proper edge-coloring of $G$ contains a rainbow copy of the path on $d$ edges.

This is an average-degree analogue of the Erdős–Sós conjecture and a rainbow conjecture proposed in the cited work. Even for subgraphs of hypercubes, the assertion remains open for $d\ge 5$.

361551.title: Weighted Berge–Fulkerson matching conjecture for bridgeless cubic graphs
361551.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a weighted bridgeless cubic graph, meaning that $G$ has no bridges, every vertex has degree $3$, and its edges have non-negative weights. Let $w(G)$ be the total edge weight and let $M$ be a **perfect matching**, a set of pairwise disjoint edges meeting every vertex exactly once.

**Weighted perfect-matching conjecture.** There exists a perfect matching $M$ such that

$$
w(M)\geq \frac{w(G)}{3}.
$$

This is presented as a weighted consequence of the Berge–Fulkerson conjecture and would imply the relevant case of the paper's triangle-free cubic bisection conjecture. Its general validity remains open.
361551.review_depth: targeted primary definitions, conjecture and neighbouring results; full paper not universally read
361551.mathematical_review: Source Conjecture 4.15 read. The all-1/3 vector satisfies the perfect-matching-polytope constraints: vertex sums are 1 and every odd cut has at least 3 edges (odd parity and bridgelessness). Thus some perfect matching has weight at least total/3 by averaging a convex decomposition. This is a classical Edmonds bridge, not a discovery. The 2026 journal counterpart explicitly calls the claim Theorem 2.4 (Naddef and Pulleyblank).

361656.title: The center-realization conjecture for 2-connected plane graphs
361656.literal_statement: Let $H$ be a 2-connected plane graph. A vertex $v$ of $H$ is **quasi-eccentric to** $H[f]$ for a face $f$ of $H$ when the relevant quasi-eccentricity condition holds for the subgraph induced by the boundary of $f$. **Center-realization conjecture.** If each vertex of $H$ is quasi-eccentric to $H[f]$ for some face $f$ of $H$, then there exists a plane graph $G$ such that $H$ is both the center of $G$ and an isometric subgraph of $G$. The preceding results establish sharp order bounds for maximal planar graphs, but whether the analogous sufficient-and-necessary condition extends to this broader class of 2-connected plane graphs is left as a further question.

361871.title: The extremizer conjecture for the critical Riesz projection inequality

\|P_+\psi\|_{\mathfrak{p}(q)}=\|\psi\|_q,
$$

then there are a constant $C\neq0$ and an inner function $I$ such that $\psi=CI$. The endpoint $q=1$ is described as exceptional, and the asserted characterization is conjectured for the stated non-endpoint ranges.

362578.title: Tower-growth conjecture for hereditary 3-uniform hypergraph properties

L_{\mathcal{H}}(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)\geq Tw(\epsilon_1^{-C}).

363037.title: Figueroa-Centeno et al.'s product antimagic conjecture
363037.literal_statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a connected graph of size $m$. A labeling of its edges by $\{1,2,\dots,m\}$ is **product antimagic** if the products of the labels incident with the vertices are pairwise distinct. **Figueroa-Centeno et al.'s product antimagic conjecture.** Every connected graph of size at least three is product antimagic. Product antimagic labelings were introduced by Figueroa-Centeno et al.; the conjecture is presented as an open variation of the antimagic graph problem.
363037.review_depth: targeted primary definitions, conjecture and neighbouring results; full paper not universally read
363037.mathematical_review: Source Conjecture 1.2, the literal product-label definition and pendant-edge results read. This is a 2000 conjecture, not first posed in 2024.
363037.attempts_and_coverage: All connected labeled simple graphs on 3,4,5 vertices with >=3 edges: 1,38,728 graphs. Explicit successful permutations for every graph, 1,44,1261 permutations tried. Each search was capped at 10000 permutations per graph; no graph reached that limit unresolved. outputs/finite-product.log.
363037.remaining_gap: No counterexample; a uniform proof must handle vertices without pendant support, beyond the source sufficient condition.

363188.title: The (2,2)-Conjecture for graph decompositions
363188.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph of order at least four. A **locally irregular multigraph** is a multigraph in which the endpoints of every edge have different degrees. For a subgraph $H$ of $G$, let ${}^2H$ denote the multigraph obtained by replacing each edge of $H$ by two parallel edges.

**(2,2)-Conjecture.** The graph $G$ can be decomposed into two subgraphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ such that there exist locally irregular multigraphs $M_1$ and $M_2$ satisfying

$$
G_1\subseteq M_1\subseteq {}^2G_1,
$$

$$
G_2\subseteq M_2\subseteq {}^2G_2.
$$

Equivalently, every connected graph of order at least four should have a $(2,2)$-coloring. This formulation connects locally irregular decompositions with neighbor-sum-distinguishing edge colorings; the source presents it as an open conjecture.
363188.review_depth: targeted primary definitions, conjecture and neighbouring results; full paper not universally read
363188.mathematical_review: Source Conjectures 3/4 and their equivalence to Problem 5 read. MathDB references incorrectly say refuted: the nearby refutation is of the old local-irregularity conjecture, not (2,2). Source already proves several classes including subcubic and bipartite.
363188.attempts_and_coverage: All connected labeled simple graphs of order 4 and 5: 38 and 728 graphs, with successful colour/multiplicity assignments. 274 and 12305 assignments tried. outputs/more-finite.log.
363188.remaining_gap: No counterexample. Need a general two-colour, multiplicities {1,2} construction or an exact obstruction outside known classes.
